items.title: From Healthcare Data to Actionable Intelligence: An Integrative Review and Gated Framework for Trustworthy Al-Enabled Healthcare Analytics
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background: The increasing availability of electronic health records, clinical narratives, biomedical literature, imaging, physiological signals, and patient-generated data has created substantial opportunities for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled healthcare analytics. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) can extract, summarize, synthesize, and transform heterogeneous healthcare information. However, AI-generated information does not automatically constitute reliable or actionable intelligence. Data quality, interoperability, provenance, hallucination, bias, validation, human oversight, workflow integration, and governance may disrupt the transition from healthcare data to responsible action. Main body: This integrative review synthesizes recent literature addressing the transformation of heterogeneous healthcare data through AI-enabled analytics and identifies conditions required for reliable and actionable use. A structured literature search was conducted, followed by title and abstract screening and targeted full-text assessment of relevant evidence. Data were organized using a predefined extraction framework covering data characteristics, AI applications, interoperability, provenance, validation, privacy, human oversight, workflow integration, governance, and outcomes. Evidence was synthesized thematically across the healthcare data-to-action pathway. The synthesis identified four interconnected requirements: data readiness, evidence traceability, output reliability, and action readiness. These requirements were integrated into the proposed Data-to-Actionable-Intelligence (D2AI) Gated Framework. The framework conceptualizes healthcare AI as a sequential pathway in which data must first be fit for purpose, generated information must remain traceable to relevant evidence, outputs must undergo task-appropriate validation, and validated insights must be integrated into accountable human workflows before they can become actionable intelligence. Short conclusion: AI-generated output should not be considered actionable intelligence by default. The D2AI framework provides a health-informatics-oriented model that connects data quality, AI transformation, evidence traceability, validation, human oversight, workflow integration, and governance. It complements existing multidimensional AI evaluation frameworks by emphasizing the sequential conditions required for healthcare information to progress from heterogeneous data to accountable action. AI, artificial intelligence; D2AI, Data-to-Actionable-Intelligence; EHR, electronic health record; FAIR, findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable; FHIR, Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources; GenAI, generative artificial intelligence; LLM, large language model; RAG, retrieval-augmented generation.

items.title: Signature Recontextualization: Mapping perturbational signatures across biological contexts
items.abstract_or_text: Perturbational transcriptomics is a powerful tool for understanding gene function and drug effects, yet predicting how perturbations manifest across different biological contexts remains a central challenge, limiting translation from model systems to clinically relevant tissues. Despite growing interest in this problem, benchmarking efforts have been hindered by inconsistent evaluation tasks, heterogeneous metrics, and limited assessment across perturbation types and biological systems. Here, we introduce a benchmarking framework for cross-context perturbation-signature prediction (a task we define as signature recontextualization), grounded in explicit definitions of the prediction task, target-data availability, and evaluation metrics centered on signature recovery. The framework evaluates prediction performance across three target-context data regimes: (1) control only, where only control profiles from the target context are measured; (2) low coverage, where a limited subset of perturbations in the target context are measured; and (3) high coverage, where most perturbations in the target context are measured. This design enables systematic assessment of how prediction performance depends on target-context sample size while providing a standardized basis for comparing methods. We evaluate newly developed projection-based (projectCor) and network-based (netProp) methods alongside deep learning-based foundation models (scGPT, STACK) and statistical baselines. The benchmark spans diverse perturbational datasets: CRISPR knockdowns and drug perturbations in cell lines, plus in vivo chemical perturbations in rat tissues from DrugMatrix, extending evaluation beyond isolated cell-line models to tissue-level responses. For each method, evaluation was limited to the datasets, and perturbation types each model supports. Across tasks, projection and network propagation approaches show strong flexibility across perturbation types and biological contexts, and in several cases match or exceed the performance of deep learning and foundation models. We further show that perturbation predictability varies substantially with pathway conservation, transcriptional response strength, and baseline similarity between source and target contexts. All datasets, methods, and evaluation utilities are released as an open-source R package (sigRecon), providing a foundation for reproducible benchmarking and future method development.

items.title: General-Purpose Vision Models to Dermatology-Specific Foundation Models: Comparative Evaluation for Facial Skin Disease Classification
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Skin diseases represent a major global health burden, while access to dermatological expertise remains limited in many rural and resource-constrained settings. These disparities have increased interest in scalable digital tools for dermatological assessment and patient education. However, trustworthy clinical AI requires reproducible evaluation, standardized benchmarking, transparent reporting of failure patterns, and assessment of model robustness across different representations and classification strategies. This study presents a systematic transfer-learning framework for six-class facial skin disease classification, comparing seven pretrained visual representations comprising ResNet50, MobileNetV3-Large, ViT-B/16, Swin-T, DINOv2, DermLIP and Derm Foundation, under a common downstream classification framework. XGBoost was used as the primary downstream classifier, while an RBF-kernel support vector machine (SVM) was additionally evaluated as an ablation analysis to investigate the dependence of classification performance on downstream classifier selection. Performance was assessed using accuracy, macro-F1, macro-AUROC, per-class recall, confusion matrices, and bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals, with paired McNemar testing and Holm correction used to compare classifier. Derm Foundation achieved the highest performance among the evaluated feature representations when combined with XGBoost, obtaining 88.17% accuracy, 88.05% macro-F1, and 98.58% macro-AUROC on the testing set. At the class level, recall was 94.5% for acne, 87.0% for atopic dermatitis, 100.0% for normal skin, 90.5% for psoriasis, 84.0% for rosacea, and 73.0% for seborrheic dermatitis. Classifier comparisons showed that the relative performance of XGBoost and RBF-SVM depended on the underlying feature representation. The principal residual classification difficulty involved seborrheic dermatitis, particularly its reciprocal confusion with rosacea. To demonstrate technical feasibility, the classification framework was integrated into a prototype Django-based web application architecture featuring an exploratory LLM module for automated patient-education content translation. Preliminary, descriptive specialist feedback was gathered to identify future engineering optimization constraints, such as inference latency and communication mechanics. These findings are limited to the evaluated testing dataset and do not establish external generalizability or clinical efficacy.

items.title: Re-evaluating the benefit of training scale in cell foundation models
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell foundation models are self-supervised neural networks pretrained on millions of cellular transcriptomes to learn representations that transfer across biological domains and downstream tasks. Despite increasing investments in model and pretraining data scale, it remains unclear how to assess whether these investments improve the quality of learned biological representations. Recent evidence from standard finetuning benchmarks suggests that cell foundation models reach performance saturation after exposure to only a fraction of the available pretraining data. We hypothesised that conventional finetuning may obscure improvements in underlying representation quality and the biological information they encoded during pretraining. To address this, we tested second- and first-generation cell foundation models across corpus sizes using standard finetuning and extended it with a comprehensive fully frozen evaluation. We found that the training-data scaling relationship becomes apparent under fully frozen finetuning, particularly for second-generation models. Zero-shot analyses similarly recovered dependence on pretraining scale. Our findings reveal a fundamental limitation of conventional foundation model evaluation and establish the importance of frozen-representation benchmarking for assessing representation quality and guiding pretraining-scale decisions.

items.title: Identifying cohorts at elevated risk of cancers using generative modeling of patient health states
items.abstract_or_text: While large language models are powerful generators of new text, forecasting disease progression from longitudinal health histories remains a challenging problem. We introduce GenEHR, an autoregressive generative model trained on electronic health records (EHRs) from millions of patients in diverse health systems. The model learns from real-world multimodal patient histories, including diagnoses, medications, lab values, and procedures while explicitly representing irregular intervals between visits to forecast future clinical events. We combine the general-purpose patient representation learned during foundational training with parameter-efficient supervised adaptation for the task of risk stratification for 17 cancer types. In five large EHR cohorts, supervised adaptation substantially improved prediction performance of a first cancer diagnosis within a five year horizon window. Our retrospective results support the prospective evaluation of GenEHR-CancerRisk as a clinical decision-support tool for prioritizing high-risk patients for screening and prevention of aggressive cancer types, such as pancreatic and ovarian cancer.

items.title: Current Attitudes and Use Patterns of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice and Medical Education Among Trauma Providers
creators: The 2026 Design for Implementation (DFI) Authorship Group,
items.abstract_or_text: Introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in clinical practice and medical education, yet uncertainty remains regarding appropriate use, oversight, and potential effects on clinical reasoning and patient safety. This study examined current LLM use patterns, attitudes, perceived risks, and priorities for responsible integration among individuals engaged in trauma care, clinical guidance development, and medical education. Methods: Participants attending the third Design for Implementation: The Future of Trauma Clinical Guidance and Research Conference (DFI) completed surveys examining LLM use, attitudes, perceived inhibitors to personal use, and clinical applications. During facilitated sessions, participants used open-ended note-taking guides to document their perspectives regarding LLM use in clinical practice, education, and guidance development. Survey data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative responses were analyzed using rapid qualitative content analysis. Results: 77 participants completed the pre-conference survey; 62 clinicians provided data regarding clinical LLM use and attitudes. Among clinicians, 15% reported daily LLM use, whereas 26% reported never using LLMs. Respondents expressed strongest agreement with the need for regular quality auditing of LLM-supported clinical decisions. Among 52 post-conference survey respondents, 96% somewhat or strongly agreed that clinical training curricula should include education on LLM use. Barriers to LLM use included time required to verify accuracy, concern about patient harm, and insufficient training in appropriate prompting. Qualitative data came from 23 note-taking documents administered during the conference. Both positive and negative perspectives arose regarding AI use, centering on topics including efficiency gains, deskilling and never-skilling, governance and oversight, accuracy and hallucination, patient safety, and education. Discussion: DFI participants recognized efficiency and informational benefits of LLMs while identifying important concerns related to accuracy, patient safety, skill development, and governance. Findings support a need for institutional guidance, education in responsible LLM use, and evaluation of the incorporation of these technologies into clinical practice and health professions education.

items.title: Extracellular Vesicles Derived from L-MYC Neural Stem Cells Mediate Neuroprotection in 3D Models of Chemotherapy- and Radiation-Induced Neurotoxicity
items.abstract_or_text: Background/Objectives: Cancer survivors frequently experience long-term neurocognitive impairments following chemotherapy and cranial irradiation, yet experimental models that enable mechanistic investigation of therapy-induced neurotoxicity at the transcriptional level remain limited. This study aimed to develop a human three-dimensional (3D) neural tissue model derived from L-Myc immortalized neural stem cells (LMNSCs) and use transcriptomic profiling to identify molecular pathways underlying chemotherapy- and radiation-induced neural injury and extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated recovery. Methods: LMNSCs were differentiated in a 3D, methylcellulose-based culture to generate neural tissue containing neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes. Cultures were exposed to methotrexate (MTX) or ionizing radiation to induce neural injury and subsequently treated with LMNSC-derived EVs. Neural injury and repair mechanisms were evaluated by immunocytochemistry and bulk transcriptomics. Results: MTX and irradiation induced dose-dependent injury, exhibited by loss of neuronal complexity and reduced glial populations. LMNSC-EV treatment promoted recovery of neuronal and glial populations following MTX- and irradiation-induced injury. Transcriptomic analysis of irradiated cultures revealed activation of inflammation, DNA damage, and stress-response pathways, which were attenuated after treatment with LMNSC-EVs. Conclusions: LMNSC-based 3D neural tissue provides a human-relevant platform for modeling cancer therapy-induced neurotoxicity. Furthermore, LMNSC-EVs represent a promising cell-free regenerative therapeutic that restores injury-associated inflammatory, stress, and metabol-ic transcriptional programs after radiation-induced neural injury.

items.title: Crystalline silica exposure causes latent biomechanical abnormalities along the cardiopulmonary axis
items.abstract_or_text: Rationale Crystalline silica exposure is a major global health burden linked to chronic lung disease and cardiopulmonary morbidity, but early lung-vascular-cardiac abnormalities preceding overt functional decline are poorly defined. Objectives To determine whether a single crystalline silica exposure produces subclinical abnormalities across the integrated axis of cardiopulmonary response (lung[->]pulmonary artery[->]right ventricle) and identify associated sex-dependent physiologic patterns and molecular programs. Methods Male and female mice received a single endotracheal instillation of crystalline silica or vehicle (saline). At 28 days, assessments included voluntary wheel running, diffusion capacity, pulmonary function testing, bronchoalveolar lavage analysis, lung histology and electron microscopy, ex vivo proximal pulmonary artery biomechanics and microstructural second harmonic generation imaging, right ventricular pressure, transthoracic echocardiography, and bulk RNA sequencing of lung and right ventricle. Results Despite recovery of body weight and preserved voluntary exercise, silica-exposed mice demonstrated reduced diffusion capacity, ultrastructural thickening, and disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier. Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed persistent inflammation with elevated macrophages, lymphocytes, neutrophils, and protein, alongside retained particulate and surfactant-rich debris (silicoproteinosis). Lung mechanics were sex-dependent; females showed a parenchymal-dominant phenotype and males showed increased airway resistance. Elevated pulmonary circulatory pressures caused increased functional stiffness and reduced distensibility of the proximal pulmonary arteries. Right ventricular free wall thickening was noted in females. Lung transcriptomics indicated persistent immune activation and extracellular matrix remodeling, while the right ventricle demonstrated metabolic reprogramming with downregulation of structural and reparative programs. Conclusions A single crystalline silica exposure induces a subclinical, multi-compartment cardiopulmonary phenotype characterized by persistent alveolar-capillary injury, pulmonary vascular stiffening, increased right ventricular afterload, sex-dependent pulmonary mechanics, and divergent organ-level transcriptomic responses.

items.title: Three Cerebellar Imaging Subtypes in Schizophrenia with Distinct Spatiotemporal Trajectories and Biological Characteristics
items.abstract_or_text: The potential role of the cerebellum in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia has received relatively insufficient attention. Prior studies characterized cerebellar abnormalities mainly at the group level, without fully considering the heterogeneity of the disease. Here, we applied a machine learning approach (Subtype and Stage Inference, SuStaIn) to cross-sectional 3D volumetric MRIs of the cerebellum, including a total of 3,550 individuals with schizophrenia (1423 females; mean age: 32.3 +/- 12.0 years) and 5,771 healthy controls (HC) (2,861 females; mean age: 32.5 +/- 12.9 years), from 34 sites worldwide. SuStaIn identified three distinct spatiotemporal trajectories in cerebellar gray matter volume reduction, respectively originating in lobule X (subtype 1), lobule III (subtype 2) and lobule VIIb (subtype 3), with subtypes 1 and 3 corresponding to the posterior lobe and subtype 2 to the anterior lobe. These trajectories were cross-sectionally inferred in 1,588 individuals with schizophrenia and replicated in another independent samples of 1,334 and 628 patients, respectively. Multimodal analyses using neuroimaging, transcriptomic and behavioral data revealed subtype-specific biological characteristics in brain morphological patterns, cerebellar-cortical connectivity, gene expression and clinical symptoms. Specifically, subtype-related genes were enriched in metabolism-related processes and immunity-related processes, respectively, in subtype 1 and subtype 2; subtype 3 showed more severe brain abnormalities and worse cognitive symptoms. Treatment data from 381 patients, with up to 12 months of follow-up, revealed poorer response to antipsychotic medications in subtype 2 and subtype 3, but better response to transcranial magnetic stimulation in subtype 1, which also had worse emotion-related symptoms. Together, our findings offer a comprehensive characterization of the heterogeneity of cerebellar pathophysiological progresses in schizophrenia, which may help in developing future clinical stratification and targeted intervention strategies.

items.title: Crop Yield Estimation With Help of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) & Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Determining Crop Yield Potential is increasingly becoming part of Intelligent Precision Agriculture Technology used to optimise management of farms, to enhance the use of resources & to achieve sustainable food production. Traditional Yield Assessment methods carried out through manual observation and statistical assessment (in most cases) require significant time, resources, and are often not effective because they do not account for the spatial variability present within agricultural fields. Therefore, this research proposes the development of an innovative intelligent crop yield prediction framework based on UAV technology, and advanced Remote Sensing & Artificial Intelligence Techniques, as an alternative to the traditional method of measurement. The current study reports on data collected from wheat fields using UAV collected high-resolution aerial photographs captured with RGB imaging cameras. The collected aerial imagery data were then processed using photogrammetric reconstruction techniques to create orthorectified maps of fields and 3D representations of wheat crops-from this data advanced image processing was performed for the purpose of Segmentation, Canopy Extraction and analysis of the Spatial Variability in Wheat Crops. UAV imagery was used to obtain various crop features (phenotypic and spectral), including: percentage of vegetation coverage, canopy texture, plant vigor, biomass characteristics, and growth variability. RGB-based vegetation indices (GLA, VARI, RGBVI, and ExG) were derived from UAV images for analysis of crop health and physiology. The extracted features were used to develop yield prediction models based on machine learning and deep learning algorithms. To predict yield, we used various predictive models (RF, SVM, DN, and LASSO). Performance of the models was compared using statistical measures such as root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that the deep learning models outperformed the other prediction algorithms, due to their ability to learn complex spatial/non-linear relationships from UAV imagery. The suggested framework offers a quick, automated, and non-destructive method of estimating agricultural yield and for use within precision agriculture. The combination of aerial imagery from UAVs (drones), analysis through GIS, and data mining through Artificial Intelligence will permit a more efficient means for monitoring agriculture and making data-driven decisions at the farm level. The results of this research highlight the benefits that can be achieved from the development and application of UAV-enabled Smart Agriculture systems in terms of increasing productivity, decreasing resource wastage, and contributing to sustainable agricultural practices.

items.title: Beyond Better Models: Barriers and a Path Forward in Generalisable TCR Antigen Specificity Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: T cells are at the centre of adaptive immunity, protecting the organism against infection and cancer. T cell receptors (TCRs), expressed on the surface of T cells, enable the recognition of target cells through interactions with peptides presented by major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) molecules. Reliable, large-scale mapping of TCRs to their cognate pMHCs remains a holy grail of modern systems immunology, with far-reaching implications for cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and the understanding and treatment of autoimmune diseases. While exhaustive experimental mapping remains intractable due to the enormous combinatorial sequence space of TCRs and pMHCs, computational approaches offer a promising alternative. Consequently, we have witnessed increasingly sophisticated computational models of TCR antigen specificity, from small neural networks to deep generative models and large protein language models. However, several independent benchmarks have shown that these models, despite their size and sophistication, largely fail to generalise to TCRs or pMHCs not present in the data available during model development. Here, we investigate possible reasons for this and suggest a path forward to generalisable TCR:pMHC prediction. First, our analysis of the largest public repositories of TCR:pMHC data reveals significant biases towards a small number of antigens and MHC molecules, sparse sampling of TCR sequence space per pMHC, as well as inconsistencies and inaccuracies in data collation. Second, we show the importance of carefully setting up model evaluation to measure discrimination based on antigen specificity instead of confounding factors present in the evaluation data. Finally, we highlight the need for and propose how best to match the evaluation metric with the specific downstream application of the predictions. Our investigation suggests that we, as a community, need more representative and better curated data, and a robust set of metrics and benchmarks to guide future model development towards generalisable TCR:pMHC specificity prediction.

items.title: A Dual-Track Knowledge Graph for Evidence-Based Pediatric Medication Management in Neurological Disorders: Implications for Rational Drug Use and Public Health Governance
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Pediatric neurological disorders represent a leading cause of chronic childhood de integrity of domestic pediatric drug indicisability and necessitate long-term standardized pharmacological intervention. Current clinical practice for pediatric neurological disorders is constrained by fragmented research evidence, incomplete pediatric drug labeling specifications, prevalent off-label drug use, and the scarcity of age-appropriate pharmaceutical formulations, resulting in inconsistent clinical medication standards and persistent pediatric medication safety risks. As an efficient tool for integrating heterogeneous biomedical data, the knowledge graph facilitates standardized medication management and evidence mining for public health research. This study constructed a dual-track knowledge graph framework centered on clinical practice guideline evidence and semantic-derived potential medication associations. The framework systematically organizes multi-dimensional medication evidence for pediatric neurological disorders, identifies critical gaps in pediatric medication resources, and provides empirical support for optimized evidence-based medication management and refined pharmaceutical public health governance. Methods This study synthesized multi-source authoritative data, including global clinical practice guidelines for pediatric neurological disorders (2008–2025), official drug approval labeling documents, and professional pharmaceutical databases. A dual-track evidence integration framework was implemented for standardized knowledge organization in pediatric neurological evidence-based medication management. The primary track extracted explicit disease–drug therapeutic associations recommended by clinical practice guidelines to form authoritative, standardized clinical medication evidence. The auxiliary track supplemented potential rational medication associations via textual semantic similarity analysis, expanding the coverage of medication evidence for pediatric neurological disorders. Multi-dimensional safety filtering rules were established to guarantee the rationality of exploratory evidence. All structured evidence was visualized and quantitatively analyzed using the Neo4j platform to elucidate the current status and structural deficiencies of existing pediatric medication resources. Results The established dual-track knowledge graph covered 32 common pediatric neurological disorders and 7,847 standardized drug specifications, encompassing 1,549 authoritative disease–drug relationships validated by clinical practice guidelines and 3,300 clinically viable latent medication associations. Quantitative analysis identified three prominent structural deficiencies in domestic medication resources for pediatric neurological disorders: insufficient officially approved pediatric drug indications for first-line therapeutic agents, severe shortages of child-adapted dosage forms, and inequitable cross-border accessibility of specialized pediatric medications. The dual-track framework achieved hierarchical classification of authoritative consensus evidence and exploratory potential evidence, enabling comprehensive integration and traceable management of evidence-based medication management resources. Conclusions This study proposed a targeted dual-track knowledge graph framework for evidence-based medication management in pediatric neurological disorders, effectively addressing the fragmentation and ungraded classification of existing pediatric medication evidence. The framework not only supports standardized clinical evidence-based medication and expands individualized medication reference schemes for complex conditions but also quantitatively identifies key gaps in pediatric drug approval, dosage form allocation, and public health resource distribution. It provides reliable empirical evidence for optimizing pediatric pharmaceutical governance, promoting rational pediatric drug use, and constructing a refined digital public health service system for pediatric medication management.

items.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Radiological Imaging: Bridging Computational Explanations and Radiological Reasoning
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is increasingly applied to radiological imaging to improve the transparency of artificial intelligence systems. However, the clinical usefulness of many XAI approaches remains uncertain because computational explanations are not always aligned with radiological reasoning, user requirements, workflow, or governance needs. This study aimed to map recent XAI research in radiological imaging, identify gaps in the clinical translation of explanations, and develop an integrative framework for clinically oriented XAI. A systematic scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O’Malley framework and subsequent refinements, with reporting guided by PRISMA-ScR. MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and Embase via Ovid were searched for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2020 and June 2026. Eligible studies applied identifiable XAI approaches to radiological or clinically relevant medical imaging and reported information concerning explanations or their evaluation. Evidence was descriptively mapped and thematically synthesized according to XAI methods, clinical applications, explanation evaluation, clinical translation, usability, workflow integration, and governance. The evidence demonstrated substantial methodological diversity across imaging modalities, clinical tasks, AI architectures, and XAI approaches. This includes gradient-based, perturbation and feature-based, attention-based, prototype and concept-based, counterfactual, and inherently interpretable approaches. However, explanation evaluation was predominantly model-centered, with comparatively limited assessment of clinical understanding, relevance, usefulness, and integration into radiological decision-making. A recurring clinical translation gap was identified between computational outputs, such as heatmaps and feature-attribution representations, and the anatomical, morphological, and diagnostic concepts used in radiological reasoning. Workflow, usability, human oversight, and governance were also inconsistently integrated into XAI evaluation. These findings indicate that the principal challenge in radiological XAI is not the absence of explanation techniques but the lack of an integrated process for selecting, translating, evaluating, and documenting explanations according to clinical context. To address this gap, the Explainability–Radiology AI Integration (XRAI) Framework was developed, comprising six linked layers: clinical context profiling, XAI method selection, explanation generation, clinical translation, usability validation and feedback, and regulatory compliance logging. XRAI provides a conceptual and a transparent basis for connecting computational explainability with clinically meaningful and accountable radiological practice. Further empirical evaluation is required to establish its effectiveness across clinical tasks, imaging modalities, user groups, and deployment environments.

items.title: EEG Biomarkers for Rett Syndrome: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning with Explainable AI
items.abstract_or_text: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by abnormal cortical activity, which can be captured using electroencephalography (EEG). Although machine learning (ML) has shown promise for diagnosing several neurological conditions, comprehensive evaluation of classical ML and deep learning (DL) methods, together with physiologically meaningful explanations, remains limited for RTT. This study analyses resting-state, eyes-closed EEG recordings from RTT patients and healthy controls using both power spectral density (PSD)-based ML and end-to-end DL frameworks. Classical ML models, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were trained on PSD features, while EEG-specific DL architectures, including ShallowConvNet, DeepConvNet, EEGNet, and EEG Conformer, were trained directly on preprocessed EEG signals. Subject-wise cross-validation was used to avoid data leakage, with balanced accuracy as the primary performance metric because it equally accounts for sensitivity and specificity. Random Forest achieved the best performance among the classical ML models, whereas EEGNet achieved the highest DL performance. An ablation study indicated that 4-second EEG epochs offered the optimal trade-off between model performance and robustness. Model interpretability was investigated using SHAP for Random Forest and occlusion sensitivity analysis for EEGNet. Both methods consistently identified delta and theta oscillations, along with centro-frontal brain regions, as key contributors to RTT classification. These findings show that both PSD-based machine learning and end-to-end deep learning methods can reliably identify RTT and highlight common neurophysiological biomarkers, offering an interpretable framework for EEG-based diagnosis and biomarker discovery for Rett Syndrome.

items.title: Major Revision, Minor Accountability: LLMs as Reviewers of Published Articles in Top-Tier Journals
items.abstract_or_text: With the growth of scientific output, the peer review system is approaching a breaking point: reviewers are increasingly hard to secure, and turnaround times lengthen accordingly. LLM-assisted or LLM-generated peer review has been proposed as a remedy, but how such models would treat manuscripts already published in top-tier journals, the closest thing the current system has to a gold standard of scientific validity, is not known. Here we assembled a corpus of 200 articles, each released under a CC BY 4.0 license and published in 2026, from 20 general-science, life-science, and clinical-medicine journals including Nature, Science, and Cell, and asked four current LLMs (two proprietary, two open-weight) to produce independent peer-review reports of each one under a blinded protocol. Their decisions were overwhelmingly harsh and starkly inconsistent with each other: 605 of 800 reviews (75.6%) recommended major revision or rejection, but the rate at which any single model did so ranged from 17.5% to 100% (p < 0.001), disagreement on manuscripts that had, by construction, already survived real editorial review at the journals in question. When the same manuscripts were doctored with one deliberately planted, field-specific methodological or statistical flaw, detection rates varied from 17.0% to 60.5% across models (p < 0.001). Recommending revision for papers that had already passed editorial review (low specificity) while missing flaws deliberately placed in front of them (low sensitivity), these models produce output that should be read for what it is: an uneven, framing- and model-dependent signal.

items.title: IndoNutriQA: An Indonesian Clinical Nutrition Question Answering Benchmark
items.abstract_or_text: Clinical Question Answering (QA) underpins Clinical Intelligent Decision Support Systems, but progress is severely limited for low-resource languages such as Indonesian by the absence of public domain-specific data. We introduce IndoNutriQA, an expert-curated Indonesian clinical QA benchmark of 911 question-answer pairs built from real clinical-nutrition reports. Rather than a large-scale training corpus, it is positioned as a high-quality evaluation resource: every pair is grounded in a clinically relevant context, enriched with structured metadata (anthropometric assessment, medical diagnosis, document provenance, chunk segmentation). Eight standardised question types following the Nutrition Care Process (NCP), including the Problem, Etiology, Sign and Symptom (PES) diagnosis statement, are answered for every report, which was written by a graduate-level dietetic intern, by one of three nutritionists. Answers are free-form clinical prose rather than extractive spans, and an expert validation study finds 6-10% of reference answers contestable. The dataset supports generative, extractive and retrieval-augmented QA as well as zero- and few-shot LLM evaluation. We report fine-tuned baselines (IndoBERT variants, mT5, RAG) with 5-fold cross-validation, learning curves and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and benchmark eight contemporary LLMs zero- and five-shot. We further calibrate our LLM-as-judge rubric against three expert raters (one RD, two nutritionists), finding it human-comparable on factuality and completeness but unreliable on clinical safety, and a human error analysis shows it misses unsupported content that the raters identify. IndoNutriQA is released to foster research in Indonesian clinical NLP and nutritional decision support.

items.title: Neuro-Metabolic and Vascular Dysregulation are Functional Biomarkers of Acquired Brain Injury
creators: Chong Chie, J. A. K. H.
items.abstract_or_text: Emerging clinical and neuropathological evidence suggests a direct link between traumatic brain injury (TBI) and neurodegenerative diseases (ND), but the mechanisms by which TBI contributes to ND onset and progression remain unclear. To bridge this gap, the NINDS TBI-ADRD consortium developed a diagnostic framework to guide the design and evaluation of TBI-ADRD experiments using translational neuroimaging (DCE-MRI, 18F-FDG-PET) and advanced image-processing pipelines. Neuro-metabolic and vascular dysregulation (MVD) and metabolic functional connectomics (MFC) were evaluated in 8-month C57BL/6J mice at 30- and 60-days post-injury (DPI). Both MVD and MFC revealed significant changes at 30- and 60-DPI that were sex- and injury side-dependent. Female mice showed greater regional MVD alterations, while MFC identified sex-dependent changes at 30-DPI that diminished by 60-DPI. These findings suggest that a single mid-life closed-head injury induces sexually dimorphic MVD and brain network remodeling, supporting the potential of MVD as a sensitive biomarker for improved clinical monitoring post-TBI.

items.title: Comparative evaluation of large language models for guideline-based oral cancer management: a standardized assessment of GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, and Grok-3
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being investigated as tools for clinical information synthesis, patient education, and decision support. However, fluent language generation does not necessarily translate into clinically accurate or guideline-concordant recommendations. The extent to which contemporary LLMs can translate evidence-based oral cancer guidance into patient-accessible information and individualized clinical management remains insufficiently characterized. Methods We developed a standardized evaluation framework based on the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2025. GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, and Grok-3 were evaluated in two tasks: guideline summarization for non-medical audiences and case-based oral cancer management. Model outputs were assessed by three oral and maxillofacial surgeons across predefined dimensions, including accuracy, clarity, conciseness, logical coherence, diagnostic accuracy, treatment-regimen appropriateness, surgical planning, radiotherapy, systemic-status assessment, and prognosis. BLEU-4 and ROUGE-L were treated as exploratory text-similarity metrics. Results In the guideline-summary task, DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest reported overall assessment score (8.8/10), followed by GPT-4o (8.3/10) and Grok-3 (7.8/10). DeepSeek-R1 also achieved the highest reported scores for accuracy (9.0), clarity (8.7), conciseness (8.7), and logic (9.2). In the case-based task, DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest reported comprehensive score (87.44), followed by Grok-3 (77.77) and GPT-4o (68.61). DeepSeek-R1 achieved high reported scores for treatment-regimen accuracy (92), surgical-resection accuracy (93), radiotherapy-dose assessment (98), and prognosis (97). Grok-3 achieved the highest reported radiotherapy-dose score (100). The raw dataset also contains several anomalous values that require verification before inferential analysis, including a reported ROUGE-L value of 207 and several clinical scores of 20. Conclusions The three LLMs demonstrated distinct performance profiles rather than a uniformly superior model. DeepSeek-R1 showed the strongest descriptive overall performance in the current benchmark, particularly for structured treatment planning and prognostic assessment. However, clinically relevant variability was observed in staging, lymph-node management, surgical extent, HPV contextualization, and unsupported specificity. LLMs should therefore be considered assistive rather than autonomous clinical decision-support technologies. Larger multicentre studies using expert consensus standards and clinically meaningful endpoints are warranted.

items.title: A Plasmodium falciparum Pangenome Resource to Drive Structural Variant Discovery and to assist Malaria Control
items.abstract_or_text: Plasmodium falciparum, the deadliest causative agent of malaria, harbours extensive structural variation that underlies key biological processes including drug resistance and diagnostic evasion. Here, we present PfPan, a P. falciparum pangenome constructed from 13 geographically diverse high-quality reference genomes using Minigraph-Cactus, adding 4.77 Mb of sequence beyond the 3D7 linear reference. We identify over 5,000 structural variants (SVs) across the reference genomes and demonstrate improved genotyping using the vg toolkit compared to linear reference-based approaches, with comparable performance for small variant discovery. Benchmarking against assembly-derived truth sets confirms pangenome superiority for structural variant detection, particularly at complex and hypervariable loci. Applying PfPan to 878 globally sampled P. falciparum whole-genome sequences, we characterise biologically and clinically relevant SVs, including the complex drug resistance-linked gch1 locus, and explore deletions upstream of the coding sequence for the diagnostic target HRP2. PfPan provides a foundational resource for mitigating reference bias in P. falciparum genomic surveillance and establishes a framework for improved detection of variants associated with drug resistance and malaria control in monoclonal P. falciparum samples that have not undergone selective whole-genome amplification.

items.title: Limb-localized induction of regeneration reshapes brain and amputation-site transcriptional states in adult Xenopus laevis
items.abstract_or_text: Limb regeneration requires coordinated tissue reconstruction and nervous system reintegration, yet whether regenerative induction alters brain responses to limb loss remains unclear. We analyzed transcriptomics from the paired brains and amputation sites of adult Xenopus laevis after hindlimb amputation with or without a 24 hour exposure to localized, pro-regenerative multi-drug treatment (MDT) delivered through a wearable bioreactor device. At 24 hours post treatment (24 HPT), MDT brains showed increased vascular and basement membrane transcripts and enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation and mTORC1 programs. In the limb, an exploratory integrated stress response (ISR) score increased at 11 and 24 HPT and returned to control levels by 7 days post-treatment (7 DPT), coinciding with induction of growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15), a cytokine responsive to mitochondrial stress. We detected no corresponding increase in brain ISR score. At 7 DPT, MDT brains showed enrichment of immune, heme metabolism and biosynthetic programs, reduced synaptic transmission gene expression, and increased gdf15.L. Relative to an external uninjured reference, MDT and amputation only brains showed concordant changes, with treatment modifying selected programs. Cross-species comparative analyses identified partial overlap with an axolotl regenerative glutamatergic signature and separation from selected mammalian injury profiles. These findings reveal cross-tissue responses to regenerative induction and identify candidate mechanisms of brain body communication in biomedically engineered vertebrate limb regeneration.

items.title: Alzheimer's Disease-Associated Proteomic Changes in Olfactory Stem Cells Show Pathway-Level Transcriptomic Overlap
items.abstract_or_text: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive, neurodegenerative disorder and the leading cause of dementia worldwide. Although recent therapeutic advances have provided some disease-modifying potential, there is currently no curative treatment for AD, highlighting the need for improved disease models and early biomarkers. Olfactory mucosal stem cells, which can be expanded in vitro as olfactory neurosphere-derived (ONS) cells, represent a promising source for biomarker discovery because olfactory tissue is more accessible than central nervous system tissue and has been reported to exhibit AD-related pathological changes. In this study, we used subcellular fractionation-based proteomics, reconstructed bulk proteomics and integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analyses to characterise alterations in ONS cells derived from healthy control, mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD individuals. Fraction-specific proteomics identified cytoplasmic and nuclear-enriched protein abundance changes, including alterations in proteins and pathways associated with cytoskeletal organisation, RNA processing, intracellular trafficking, autophagy and mitochondrial/metabolic processes. Reduced LC3B abundance in cytoplasmic AD ONS cells was supported by western blot analysis, although LC3B abundance alone does not indicate altered autophagic flux. Reconstructed bulk proteomics identified 40 FDR-significant proteins in AD compared with HC, defining an AD-associated protein signature enriched for extracellular matrix, cytoskeletal, organelle-associated and RNA-processing pathways. Despite proteomic enrichment of mitochondrial and metabolic pathways, Seahorse Mito Stress Test analysis did not identify significant group-level differences in mitochondrial respiration. Integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analysis revealed partial RNA-protein concordance and pathway-level overlap across disease-associated processes. Together, these findings support the use of patient-derived ONS cells as a model for investigating AD- and MCI-associated molecular changes and highlight protein signatures for further validation.

items.title: Scalable subclonal reconstruction of cancer cells in DNA sequencing data using a penalized likelihood model
items.abstract_or_text: Background Characterizing intratumor heterogeneity and subclonal architecture from bulk DNA sequencing provides important insights into cancer evolution. However, existing subclonal reconstruction methods remain computationally demanding, hindering iterative quality control and reproducible application across large genomic cohorts. Methods Distinct from existing likelihood-based and Bayesian approaches, we developed CliPP (Clonal structure identification through Pairwise Penalization), utilizing machine learning to add pairwise fusion penalty to the full likelihood, in order to simultaneously estimate mutation cellular prevalence and fuse compatible estimates into clusters without prespecifying the number of clusters. We benchmarked CliPP in three simulation datasets comprising 5,256 tumors for accuracy, and further evaluated its concordance with consensus calls in 2,008 tumors profiled by whole-genome sequencing from the Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes (PCAWG) study. We then applied a standardized, quality-controlled workflow to whole-exome sequencing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), yielding a high-confidence cohort of 5,424 tumors across 31 cancer types. Within this cohort, we mapped the clonality of 13,960 high-confidence driver mutations in 4,375 tumors. Results CliPP showed competitive performance across all datasets, as compared to PhylogicNDT and PyClone-VI, while gaining significant improvement in speed. In PCAWG, CliPP achieved a concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) of 0.93 with the published consensus, leading to a 96.3% agreement in driver-level clonal/subclonal assignments from the PCAWG study (Cohen's kappa = 0.81). It took approximately one hour for CliPP to complete the analysis of the entire PCAWG and TCGA cohorts, gaining noticeable time over existing methods. Applying CliPP to the TCGA cohort, we generate a complete annotation of driver clonality across TCGA samples, and observe broad patterns of driver timing that recapitulate known biology. The CliPP-on-Web app allows non-computational researchers to directly obtain subclonal annotations of their tumor samples. Conclusions Machine learning assisted CliPP combines competitive reconstruction accuracy, substantial computational efficiency, and standardized quality control to enable reproducible subclonal reconstruction at large scale. Its pan-cancer application characterizes context-dependent patterns of driver clonality, and its software web interface enables cancer evolution inquiries from the cancer research community.

items.title: QSGT: Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer for Faithful Multi-modal Radiology Report Summarization
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Improving the alignment between visual evidence andtextual descriptions in medical vision-language models(VLM) remains a critical challenge for achieving entitylevelfaithfulness in low-resource generation tasks. Thispaper proposes Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer(QSGT), a hybrid approach of token pruningand mixture of experts (MoE), grounded on the conceptionof quantum many-body wavefunction. This hybridapproach was aimed at improving the selectionof both modality-specific expert tokens and the formationof non-dominating experts to determine stableconjugates. The token pruning approach was improvedusing the quantum orbital style token assignments andthe mixture of experts by the quantum doubly occupancyapproximation. We also introduce two clinicallymotivated regularization terms, pair loss and seniorityloss, further enforce semantic consistency and dominanceof diagnostically relevant features. Our extensiveexperiments across seven thoracic disease categoriesdemonstrate that QSGT significantly outperforms stateof-the-art medical VLMs on multiple evaluation metrics,including RadGraph (36.2), SPICE (42.68), andconsistently high BERTScore (98), on the MIMIC-CXRtest set. QSGT achieves substantial gains in clinical correctnessand semantic accuracy, particularly for complexconditions such as pneumonia and pneumothorax. Ablationstudies confirmthe importance of each architecturalcomponent, while convergence analyses show stable andinterpretable learning dynamics. These results indicate that QSGT provides a robust and clinically meaningfulsolution for multimodal medical report summarization,enabling more reliable, interpretable, and patientcentredclinical AI systems.

items.title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
items.abstract_or_text: As wearable and digital health systems increasingly generate longitudinal physiological records, communicating these observations in patient-accessible language remains a significant challenge. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising mechanism for translating structured clinical information into readable narratives, but this process may introduce semantic drift, where clinically precise meaning is distorted during simplification. We investigate evidence-grounded health summarization for menstrual health monitoring using a constrained generation framework that combines structured evidence conditioning with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using a prompt-based constrained generation framework. We evaluate semantic alignment using Natural Language Inference (NLI), atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures. Across three LLMs and 4,500 generated summaries, explicit grounding constraints consistently improve clinical alignment, particularly by improving uncertainty preservation and, once faithfulness is evaluated against retrieved evidence, generally preserving or improving faithfulness, while effects on omission remain model-dependent. We also find that improved clinical alignment comes at the cost of increased reading difficulty and medical terminology. These findings highlight the need to jointly evaluate faithfulness, uncertainty preservation, and readability when developing patient-facing medical LLM systems.

items.title: Development of a deep learning model for glomerulus detection and segmentation in kidney histopathology images
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Estimation of nephron number, an indicator of renal reserve, requires quantitative assessment of glomerular number and size in kidney biopsy specimens. We aimed to develop an automated system for quantitative measurement of glomerular areas from clinical kidney biopsy images, across diverse kidney diseases. Methods: We developed a two-stage deep learning system combining Faster R-CNN for glomerular detection in whole-slide images (WSIs) and DeepLabV3+ for segmentation. Of 114 kidney biopsies (228 WSIs), 104 were used for model development and 10 for independent final evaluation. Agreement was assessed using the F1-score for detection, the Dice coefficient for segmentation, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for glomerular area measurement. Analysis was performed at 40x total magnification (2.331 m/pixel) and validated against 400x images. Results: In the independent evaluation set, the artificial intelligence (AI) model achieved a mean F1-score of 0.851 for detection, compared with 0.888 among experts. For segmentation, the Dice coefficient was 0.959 {+/-} 0.011 and the per-pair ICC (2,1) for area measurement was 0.989 {+/-} 0.009; both were comparable to inter-expert agreement. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -344 m2 (95% limits of agreement, -1904 to 1216 m2) between 40x and 400x measurements. Conclusion: The two-stage model achieved glomerular segmentation and area measurement comparable to expert agreement in independent clinical data, with detection performance approaching inter-expert agreement, and provided reliable measurements at low magnification. This automated approach may facilitate large-scale quantitative kidney pathology and nephron number estimation from clinical kidney biopsies.

items.title: Evaluation of the Use of White Vinegar as an Alternative Agent in the Histological Detection of Digestive System Organs
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Traditional formaldehyde fixation poses severe health and environmental risks, necessitating the investigation of eco-friendly alternatives. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of natural white vinegar (an acetic acid-based bio-fixative) as a sustainable, cost-effective, and low-toxicity alternative to formalin in routine histotechnological processes. Liver, pancreas, and ileum tissues obtained from 18 male Wistar Albino rats (8 weeks old) were randomly assigned to three fixation groups: Control (10% Neutral Buffered Formalin [NBF]), Experiment 1 (Pure White Vinegar), and Experiment 2 (Formalin + White Vinegar combination). Following routine tissue processing, sections were stained with hematoxylin-eosin (H&E), Masson’s trichrome, and toluidine blue. Semi-quantitative scoring was performed blindly by six independent histologists based on tissue integrity, cellular morphology, and staining homogeneity. Digital image analysis was conducted via optical density quantification using ImageJ software, and statistical evaluations were performed using SPSS (p 0.05 overall). ImageJ densitometric analysis demonstrated that color and optical density distributions were statistically similar across all groups (p > 0.05), confirming that vinegar fixation did not adversely affect dye-binding capacity. Histological and digital densitometric analyses demonstrate that white vinegar successfully preserves tissue and cellular integrity at a level comparable to formalin. These findings suggest that white vinegar-based formulations hold strong potential as sustainable, bio-safe, and cost-effective alternative fixatives in routine histotechnology.

items.title: Preoperative diffusion-perivascular MRI burden and postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation in Parkinson disease
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation may reflect pre-existing brain vulnerability, but the preoperative imaging correlates of this vulnerability remain uncertain. We examined whether a combined diffusion and perivascular imaging burden was associated with delirium after bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation. This single-centre observational cohort included 100 patients with Parkinson disease undergoing bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation and 32 healthy controls scanned with the same preoperative MRI protocol. Delirium was assessed during postoperative days using the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale with clinical adjudication. Age- and sex-adjusted reference models fitted in healthy controls were used to standardise tract diffusion metrics, diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space, and basal ganglia enlarged perivascular space counts. Directionally aligned diffusion and perivascular scores were averaged with equal domain weights. Patients who developed postoperative delirium (n = 30) had higher combined burden than those who did not (n = 70; 95% CI, 0.584 to 1.526; q

items.title: Functional Validation of Known BEST1 Variants Using a Robust Halide-Sensitive YFP Quenching Assay
items.abstract_or_text: Bestrophinopathies comprise a heterogeneous group of inherited retinal degenerative diseases caused by mutations in the Bestrophin-1 (BEST1) gene. Although more than 250 pathogenic BEST1 variants have been reported, only a small subset has undergone functional interrogation. OPGx-BEST1 is an investigational gene therapy designed to restore BEST1 function through augmented wild-type BEST1 expression in retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells. Previous studies in animal models and patient-derived cellular systems have demonstrated that loss-of-function (LOF) BEST1 variants can be complemented with wild-type protein expression and are therefore amenable to gene augmentation strategies. In contrast, known gain-of-function (GOF) mutations appear to retain pathogenic activity despite augmentation with wild-type BEST1. Therefore, given the therapeutic relevance of LOF/GOF disease mechanisms in bestrophinopathies, a comprehensive genotype-phenotype characterization across the BEST1 mutational landscape is critical to inform clinical trial enrollment. Conventional approaches to profile BEST1 variants have relied upon patient-derived RPE models and electrophysiologic assessment of channel function. While these systems provide valuable translational insight, they lack the scalability, speed, and experimental flexibility needed for a systematic evaluation of many variants for patient selection. Here, we describe a functional screening platform that leverages an engineered halide-sensitive reporter cell line to quantitatively assess the activity of BEST1 mutant proteins.

items.title: The effectiveness, cost consequences, and safety of 5 versus 7 days of oral flucloxacillin for lower limb cellulitis in adults presenting in UK primary care: study protocol for the COAT trial - a pragmatic, multicentre, double-blind, randomised, phase 3 non-inferiority trial
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Cellulitis is an acute bacterial infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, most commonly affecting the lower limbs. UK guidelines recommend a 5–7-day course of oral flucloxacillin as first-line treatment in primary care. Most patients are prescribed a 7-day course or longer. Evidence supporting shorter regimens is limited and largely derived from hospital-based studies using alternative antimicrobial agents. No trials have evaluated different durations of oral flucloxacillin in primary care. This trial aims to assess the effectiveness, safety, and cost consequences of 5 versus 7 days of oral flucloxacillin for lower limb cellulitis in UK primary care. Methods This is a pragmatic, phase III, multi-centre, randomised, double-blind, non-inferiority trial, with internal pilot and parallel health economic evaluation. Adults (≥18 years) with lower-limb cellulitis will be randomised (1:1) to 5 vs 7 days of oral flucloxacillin, operationalised by providing 500 mg flucloxacillin or matched placebo, four times daily for two days following completion of a 5-day standard-of-care course of open-label flucloxacillin. Participants will be followed up for 28 days using self-reported symptom diaries and at 12 months through medical notes review. The primary outcome is pain over days 6–14 post-baseline, recorded daily on a 0–10 Numerical Rating Scale. Secondary outcomes include total antibiotic and analgesic use, patient-reported wellbeing, health-related quality of life, severity of leg swelling and redness, time to self-reported recovery, healthcare resource use (including hospital admissions, primary care consultations, and medication), recurrent cellulitis episodes, complications, and participant-incurred costs. The primary analysis will compare pain scores between groups using a generalised linear mixed model, adjusting for baseline pain and stratification variables and accounting for clustering of repeated measures within participants. The trial received ethical approval from the North East – Tyne & Wear South Research Ethics Committee on 16 June 2023 (ref: 23/NE/0021). Trial registration ISRCTN27053187, 01/06/2023, https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN27053187

items.title: Antibacterial, antibiofilm, modulatory effects, pharmacokinetic profile, toxicity and molecular docking of Monarda fistulosa essential oil against Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract The increasing spread of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii strains and their high biofilm-forming capacity represent a serious global public health challenge, limiting therapeutic options. Given this scenario, the aim of this study was to evaluate the chemical composition, antibacterial and antibiofilm activity, modulatory effect in combination with carbapenems and ciprofloxacin, and in silico interaction mechanisms of Monarda fistulosa essential oil (MFEO) against nosocomial isolates of MDR A. baumannii , as well as to predict pharmacokinetic and toxicity characteristics. Phytochemical characterization via Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) identified the monoterpene geraniol (92.3%) as the major constituent. Broth microdilution assays demonstrated significant antibacterial activity of MFEO, with Minimum Inhibitory Concentrations (MIC) ranging from 312 to 625 µg/mL and a bactericidal profile against all tested strains. In the synergism evaluation using the checkerboard method, MFEO exhibited an additive effect with meropenem and imipenem, reducing the carbapenem dosage required to inhibit bacterial growth in the most resistant strains, although it showed an indifferent interaction with ciprofloxacin. Furthermore, MFEO demonstrated strong dose-dependent inhibition during the initial cell adhesion phase and promoted significant eradication of pre-formed mature biofilms, outperforming meropenem control treatments at MIC, 2xMIC, and 4xMIC concentrations. In silico analyses indicated favorable pharmacokinetic profiles and low toxicity for the MFEO compounds, while molecular docking revealed moderate binding affinity of the compounds to the catalytic residues of OXA-24 and to the outer membrane protein A (OmpA). Taken together, these results demonstrate the potential of MFEO as a phytotherapeutic agent and as a promising adjuvant in combating severe infections caused by MDR A. baumannii .

items.title: CCTP-Atlas: Compartment-Resolved Ciliary Transcriptional Dysregulation in Tetralogy of Fallot, A Six-Dataset Integrative Meta-Analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Background. Primary cilia coordinate Hedgehog-dependent outflow tract morphogenesis. Concurrent human genetics implicates ciliary loss-of-function in nonsyndromic tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) risk, yet compartment-resolved ciliary transcriptional programmes in public TOF snRNA-seq remain unmapped at module resolution. Methods. We curated a Cardiac Ciliary Transcriptomic Panel (CCTP; 1,611 genes; four modules) and executed a ten-phase integrative pipeline on six public sc/snRNA-seq resources. Differentially expressed gene tables were harmonised (adjusted p < 0.05; |log2FC| [≥] 0.5 where available), mapped to CCTP modules, and tiered by evidence strength. Patient-level pseudobulk (three TOF versus five donors), permutation-validated Compartment Dysregulation Index (CMDI), Cross-Species Concordance Score (CSCS), STRING protein-protein interaction analysis, and diffusion pseudotime on 17,290 Ho organoid cells were performed. Results. Among 1,263 unique CCTP-associated hits, 396 genes recurred in at least two dataset tables (exploratory tier; Tier A endothelial anchor n = 24 from Zulibiya et al.). Only Zulibiya endothelial M1 structural-assembly CMDI exceeded a module-size-matched permutation null (p = 0.015). Patient-level pseudobulk returned zero false-discovery-rate-significant CCTP genes. CCTP-conditioned overlap with recent ciliary genetics was non-significant (Fisher p {approx} 0.13). Ho organoid pseudotime showed highest M1/M2 activity at day 8, declining toward day 21. Genome-wide CSCS classified 11 genes as fully conserved and 136 as partially conserved among scoreable orthologs. Conclusions. Ciliary transcriptional correlates in TOF are compartment-specific and module-structured, with the strongest inferential signal in TOF endothelium (M1). CCTP-Atlas provides a reproducible, tiered prioritisation resource linking public TOF snRNA-seq, organoid maturation proxies, and partial cross-species patterns. Findings are hypothesis-generating and complement but do not replicate recent ciliary genetics evidence until expanded cohorts and functional validation are performed. Data availability. Processed gene lists, manifests, and scripts. Source datasets: GSE203274, GSE168464, GSE166462, GSE126128; Li et al. (2025) supplementary tables. This is a preprint and has not been peer-reviewed.

items.title: GeoSinkhorn Flow: Geometry-Aware Flow Matching for Perturbation-Conditioned Dynamics in Single cell Data Phenoscapes
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell technologies increasingly enable large-scale profiling of complex biological systems across many experimental perturbations, but understanding how a system reorganizes across an entire space of conditions is difficult to interpret from single-cell embeddings alone. Phenoscapes address this by embedding entire cell-state distributions, rather than individual cells, as points in a data-driven landscape. Thus, a single dot represents one experimental condition rather than one cell, yielding a map of the perturbation or patient landscape that reveals how phenotype varies continuously across conditions. Phenoscapes remain a comparatively new and underexplored representation and existing static phenoscapes position experimental conditions relative to one another without specifying trajectories that describe how a cellular population moves from one condition to another. Flow- and trajectory-based models for single-cell data are numerous, but existing approaches operate at the level of individual cells, are not built to respect the geometry of a phenoscape, and typically cannot generalize their predicted flows to conditions not seen during training. Here we introduce GeoSinkhorn Flow, a perturbation-conditioned, geometry-aware flow-matching framework specialized designed to convert a static phenoscape into a dynamic phenoscape, in which each condition-level point is additionally connected by geodesic, condition-aware transport trajectories that are consistent with the phenoscape's underlying geometry. GeoSinkhorn Flow can also model transitions directly between time points without constructing a phenoscape. GeoSinkhorn Flow uses heat-diffusion geometry to define manifold-aware transport costs and trains a geometric autoencoder whose latent Euclidean distances stay aligned with the static phenoscape geometry while extending it to unseen cells. By explicitly conditioning the learned transport dynamics on perturbation-specific gene or drug embeddings, GeoSinkhorn Flow generalizes its trajectories to new measurement conditions, produces intermediate progression states along a trajectory, and extends predictions to unseen cells and held-out perturbations. An unbalanced optimal transport variant further learns growth or transition weights, so that changes in relative cell-state abundance or transition propensity are modeled together with state movement. Across synthetic manifolds, patient-derived organoid drug responses, Perturb-seq knockdowns, and time-resolved CyTOF signaling, GeoSinkhorn Flow recovered intrinsic manifold geometry, inferred biologically coherent response trajectories, and generalized to held-out drug combinations, perturbation genes, and time points. Together, these results establish GeoSinkhorn Flow as a perturbation-conditioned, phenoscape-consistent dynamical framework, distinct from standard flow-matching approaches, for converting static phenoscapes into dynamic ones that generalize across experimental conditions.

items.title: Overcoming segmentation bottlenecks in brain tissue for spatial proteomic inference at population scale
items.abstract_or_text: In spatial proteomics across large cohorts, downstream estimates from tens of thousands of images depend on accurate cell segmentation. Yet pretrained segmentation models struggle with morphologically complex cell bodies in human brain tissue, and how domain adaptation affects downstream discovery remains unclear. Here, we introduce SPInfer, a workflow for spatial proteomic inference developed using 5,832 manually annotated cell bodies from 120 immunofluorescence images of the human prefrontal cortex. After benchmarking eight segmentation methods spanning classical, convolutional, and foundation models, we adapted Cellpose-SAM, raising cell segmentation F1 from 0.37 to 0.84 and recovering cell compositions concordant with matched single-nucleus RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics. Across 14,765 images from 69 postmortem donors, identical Alzheimer's disease pathology models found no significant associations after false discovery rate correction using zero-shot masks, versus four using fine-tuned masks; three linked higher OLIG2-positive fractions to greater neurofibrillary tangle and plaque burden. Using the fine-tuned masks, a graph attention network over nuclear neighborhoods classified four cell types without marker information, and differential expression analysis linked cell morphology to gene expression. This provides a pipeline for fine-tuning foundation models to segment complex tissues, enabling biological discovery in spatial proteomics at the population scale.

items.title: Spatial uncoupling of endothelial calcium signaling from phospha-tidylserine externalization in vascular injury
items.abstract_or_text: Ca2+ is both the signal that spreads injury information through the endothelium and the trigger for phospholipid scrambling that makes a membrane procoagulant. How a blood vessel can disseminate the first without broadcasting the second is unknown. Here, we combine single-cell laser injury in endothelial monolayers with imaging of intact mesenteric vessels in vitro and intravital Ca2+ imaging in vivo. Injury generated a coherent Ca2+ wavefront that spread rapidly before progressively slowing and terminating at a reproducible boundary 197 {+/-} 7 m from the wound, engaging 50 {+/-} 8 cells. The first ring of neighboring cells exhibited a distinct response that was prevented by carbenoxolone, whereas propagation beyond this ring required extracellular ATP, purinergic receptor activation, and IP3-dependent Ca2+ release. Wavefront kinematics were consistent with ATP diffusion. In vivo, injury elicited vasoconstriction and bidirectional Ca2+ waves propagating 205 {+/-} 28 m before terminating. Remarkably, despite widespread Ca2+ elevations, phosphatidylserine (PS) externalization remained confined to the wounded cell in monolayers and intact vessels in vitro. In contrast, ionomycin-induced Ca2+ overload exposed phosphatidylserine in nearly all endothelial cells. These findings reveal an unexpected spatial uncoupling between endothelial Ca2+ signaling and phospholipid scrambling, demonstrating that Ca2+ dependent scramblase activation is subject to additional spatial regulation. The endothelium can therefore propagate injury signals across a broad field of cells while maintaining a highly localized procoagulant membrane response.

items.title: APOE ε4 carriage is associated with pallido-putaminal diffusion alterations in early Parkinson’s disease
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract APOE ε4 may influence Parkinson’s disease (PD) progression, but its microstructural correlates remain unclear. We examined 75 early drug-naïve PD patients (25 ε4 carriers) and 46 healthy controls (HC; 16 ε4 carriers) from the Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative using ROI and voxel-wise diffusion tensor imaging analyses. Within PD, ε4 carriers showed higher pallidal mean, radial and axial diffusivity and lower pallidal and putaminal fractional anisotropy. Voxel-wise analyses localized differences to left pallido-putaminal clusters. HC showed no significant APOE -related differences. In exploratory analyses across the overall PD sample, higher cluster radial diffusivity was associated with higher serum neurofilament light chain at baseline (β = 0.395, p = 0.001) and across two years, without evidence of moderation by APOE genotype or association with longitudinal change. These findings link APOE ε4 to regional diffusion differences in early PD without detectable subcortical volume differences. Their disease specificity and prognostic relevance remain to be established.

items.title: Deep Learning for Random Objects in Metric Spaces: Beyond Manifold Assumptions
items.abstract_or_text: Deep learning (DL) methods have substantially improved predictive performance across a wide range of downstream prediction tasks, enabling new discoveries in multiple domains. However, principled DL methods for non-Euclidean random objects remain relatively scarce, despite the growing importance of modern biomedical outcomes taking the form of probability distributions, random graphs, functions, and other random objects in metric spaces. Motivated by a new generation of digital and clinical biomarkers, we propose a deep learning framework for regression with random objects in metric spaces. Our approach operates directly on the metric structure of the response space, avoiding restrictive manifold or Euclidean embedding assumptions imposed by many existing methods. At the same time, it retains modern statistical guarantees under the stated statistical assumptions. We establish statistical consistency and convergence rates for the proposed estimator, and characterize conditions under which it can mitigate the curse of dimensionality for hierarchically compositional regression functions. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate competitive predictive performance, with gains over several competing approaches in multiple Euclidean and non-Euclidean configurations. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of the proposed framework in two digital health case studies with distribution-valued outcomes in Wasserstein spaces, using high-resolution accelerometry and continuous glucose monitoring data. Embedding-based deep-learning methods may be less suitable when no informative low-dimensional representation exists or when the learned embedding does not adequately preserve the intrinsic geometry of the response space.

items.title: ReflectPO: Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.abstract_or_text: With external tools, large language models (LLMs) can tackle complex tasks through sustained environmental interaction. LLM-based agents are therefore increasingly used to tackle complex long-horizon tasks in real-world environments. However, these tasks involve sequential, interdependent decisions and changes in environmental states. Early execution errors affect subsequent interaction histories and environmental states, and their effects accumulate along the decision chain. To address this challenge, we propose Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization (ReflectPO), a reinforcement learning framework for autonomous error recovery in long-horizon tasks. ReflectPO comprises two core components. The first is Reflection-Guided Sampling. We use branch differences and repeated visits in interaction trajectories to construct hints for error recovery. The second is Tree-Structured Credit Assignment. We organize sampled trajectories into trees and assign action-level credit using parent--child reward differences and recovery gains. Experiments over two long-horizon tool-use benchmarks show that ReflectPO outperforms multiple existing baselines in most domains. It also achieves the best overall performance on average. Further analyses show that ReflectPO effectively improves agents' ability to recognize their own deviations, recover from erroneous states, and continue making progress toward task completion.

items.title: From Clinical Judgment to Checkable Rules: Clinician-Led Guardrails for Mental-Health Chatbots
